classification.difficultyReason: Read a piecewise-linear graph and find where it crosses the axis. Then compute signed areas with a negative part and combine them for c. No integration is needed, but signed area and sub-interval splitting add decisions.

content.prompt: The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown. Evaluate each integral.

answer.worked:
The line crosses the $x$-axis at $x=3$. The region is a rectangle plus a triangle, both above the axis.
$$\begin{align*}\int_0^3 f(x)\,dx&=2\times2+\frac12\times1\times2\\&=5\end{align*}$$

The whole region is below the $x$-axis, so its signed area is negative: a triangle plus a rectangle.
$$\begin{align*}\int_3^6 f(x)\,dx&=-\left(\frac12\times1\times2+2\times2\right)\\&=-5\end{align*}$$

Regions above the axis count positive and regions below count negative.
$$\begin{align*}\int_1^6 f(x)\,dx&=(1\times2)+\frac12(1)(2)-\frac12(1)(2)-(2\times2)\\&=2+1-1-4\\&=-2\end{align*}$$
